control_token.description: The session's control token. Required: without it the batch is rejected before any action is parsed, queued, or executed.

trace.description: Trace-recording status for this batch. Present when the session has a recorder; `degraded`/`warnings` surface best-effort recording problems so callers know the trace may be incomplete.

ActionResultReport.description: Result of one action inside a batch.

pointer.description: Round 9 / P0-9: which pointer backend/actuator realized the action (retained in the result + trace for real verification).

CancelParams.description:
`computer.cancel` request.

Cancellation is **precise**: with `request_id` set, only the request with that JSON-RPC id (on the *same connection*) is cancelled — the runtime keys the in-flight batch by `(connection_id, request_id)`, so cancelling request A never touches request B, and client A can never cancel client B's request even with an identical id. Without `request_id` the whole session's in-flight batch is cancelled (still token-verified).

control_token.description: The session's control token — required; cancelling is a mutating op.

CapabilityTokenParams.description: Shared token fields for the remaining **cross-session** sensitive reads: `runtime.pointer`, `runtime.active_application`, `runtime.desktop_layout`. (The trace reads became session-scoped in round 6.) These methods have no `session_id`, so any valid observation or control token is accepted — the token proves the caller is a trusted client of this daemon. No token → `OBSERVATION_TOKEN_REQUIRED`; a token matching nothing → `INVALID_OBSERVATION_TOKEN`.

ClientInfo.description: Identity of the client that started a session. Recorded on the session so owners can be told apart: a client must not stop a session it did not start. `client_instance_id` distinguishes multiple processes of the same client (e.g. two Pi instances).

CoordinateSpace.description: Coordinate space a caller used when describing a location or region.

oneOf.description: Image treated as a 1000x1000 canvas; top-left is (0,0).
Raw pixels inside the captured image.

DisplayBounds.description:
Logical bounds of a display in global desktop coordinates.

On macOS the origin can be negative (a secondary display to the left/above the primary one). Width/height are logical points; the backing store is `width * scale_factor` pixels.

ErrorCode.description: Well-known structured error codes. These are the stable strings that appear in the `data.code` field of a JSON-RPC error response.

oneOf.description: Attempted to `resume` a session that is in `UserTakeover`. The user must `release` first; resume can only recover a paused session.
A request/action batch exceeded the daemon's request deadline. This is distinct from `Cancelled` (explicit cancellation): the batch was still running when the deadline hit.
Capturing the screen failed (driver/capture failure, e.g. the screen recording session dropped).
A mutating operation was attempted without a control token.
A control token was presented but did not verify. The error is deliberately non-descriptive — it must not hint whether the token was malformed, wrong-length, or simply not this session's.
A sensitive read (observe / inspect / status / trace) was attempted without an observation or control token. The session id alone grants no observation permission.
A token was presented for a sensitive read but did not verify as either the session's observation or control token. Deliberately non-descriptive, like `InvalidControlToken`.
A mutating operation targeted a session that is already stopped.
The SDK-side request deadline expired. Distinct from `ActionTimeout` (daemon-side): the client timed out waiting, and reports whether the runtime confirmed the cancellation.
The client's protocol version is incompatible with the daemon's.
`runtime.shutdown` was attempted without the daemon admin token.
An admin token was presented for `runtime.shutdown` but did not verify. Deliberately non-descriptive.
The daemon is shutting down: new requests are refused until it exits. In-flight work was cancelled (or is draining within the grace period).
The session has an app/window target, and the action's coordinate landed outside that target window's bounds. The agent should re-observe the target (or confirm the coordinate) before retrying.
The session target (app/window) is unavailable: window closed, PID changed, bundle mismatch, or window id invalidated.

A `type`/`key` action was requested while keyboard focus is not on the session's target. The default policy refuses to steal focus; the caller may re-observe or explicitly allow `focus_policy: activate_target`.
An isolated pointer operation could not be realized without touching the real system cursor, and the current pointer policy forbids physical fallback (`isolated_only`).
A drag could not be executed in isolation and physical fallback is not permitted (or the runtime does not support safe isolated drag).
Physical fallback is not allowed by the session's pointer policy or the caller did not explicitly permit it for this action.

A located scroll (x, y) was requested without coordinates in a target-scoped session. Target sessions always require explicit scroll coordinates; a locationless scroll would land at the current pointer, which may be in a different app.

Both isolated backends (Direct CG + AX) failed for this action, and physical fallback was not explicitly permitted by the caller. The caller must either set `allow_physical_fallback: true` on the action or the session's pointer policy must include `physical_allowed`.

Round 8 / P0-1 (occlusion guard): the requested coordinate belongs to the scoped target's geometry, but the target window is NOT the currently interactable topmost owner of that point (another window — same app or other app — covers it), and no isolated actuator could safely complete the action. Direct CG is forbidden, AX could not complete it, and the runtime refuses the physical fallback because it would click the covering window. Never a generic ACTION_FAILED: the agent should expose the target, re-observe, or retry.

FocusPolicy.description: How strictly keyboard focus is validated before `type`/`key`/`shortcut`.

oneOf.description: Never steal foreground/key focus. If focus is not on the target, reject with `INPUT_FOCUS_MISMATCH`.
Activate the target app/window before keyboard input (explicit opt-in).

InspectMapping.description: Mapping info that lets a model safely translate an inspect-relative coordinate back into global desktop coordinates.

global_origin.description: Global desktop point corresponding to the crop's top-left corner.

normalized_1000_origin.description: The crop's top-left corner in the original frame's normalized_1000 space.

source_image_rect.description: Where the crop sits in the original image (pixels).

observation_token.description: Observation (or control) token — required; a session id alone grants no observation permission.
Observation (or control) token — required; a session id alone grants no observation permission.
Observation (or control) token — required; a session id alone grants no observation permission.

MouseButton.description: Mouse buttons understood by the macOS driver.

control_token.description: The session's control token — accepted in place of the observation token (control includes observation).

include_image.description: When true, the response carries the image as base64. Off by default so a plain `observe` stays cheap; adapters that need pixels (MCP, vision harnesses) turn it on.

observation_token.description: The session's **observation token**. Required — observing captures the desktop; a session id alone grants no observation permission. A valid control token is accepted in its place.

coordinate_space.description: P0-6: the coordinate space the returned image's pixels are expressed in (`"normalized_1000"` — the image is treated as a 1000x1000 canvas). Present on every observe so the caller never has to guess.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image (only present when the caller requested it).

image_path.description: Absolute path to the stored image file.

target_bounds.description: P0-6: when the session is scoped to a target window, the image is a CROP of that window and this is its global logical bounds (the caller maps window coords → screen via this). `None` = full-display observe.

window_id.description: P0-6: the observed window's id, when the session is window-scoped.

PermissionIssue.description: Extra structured detail attached to a [`CuError::Permission`].

PermissionKind.description: Which macOS permission is missing. Used to generate actionable guidance.

Point.description: A 2D point in some coordinate space.

PointerExecutionResult.description: Pointer-execution detail retained in an action result (round 9 / P0-7, P0-9). The backend that actually realized the action, whether it was isolated, and how the real system cursor moved (if at all). This is used by benchmark reports and human-interrupt latency analysis — never guessed from the action type.

backend.description: The actuator that actually realized the action: `"virtual" | "direct_cg_event" | "accessibility" | "physical"`.

event_detection_latency_ms.description: P0-4: human-interrupt telemetry, present when a real human input occurred during or near this action. `human_to_input_stop_ms` is THE Human Interrupt KPI — hardware event → LAST runtime synthetic input; 0 when the agent had already stopped. `event_detection_latency_ms` is hardware event → Event Tap callback; `human_to_takeover_ms` is hardware event → takeover applied. The inverse `synthetic → human` direction is intentionally NOT exposed here (it must never be labelled as interrupt latency).

human_input_during_fallback.description: P0-2: whether a real human input occurred during the physical fallback transaction (in which case the cursor is NEVER yanked back). Absent when no physical fallback ran.

isolated.description: True when the action executed without touching the real system cursor.

physical_cursor_delta_px.description: Distance the system cursor moved (logical px); 0 for isolated actions.

physical_cursor_moved.description: True when the real system cursor was temporarily moved.

physical_cursor_restored.description: Whether the cursor was restored to its original position after a physical fallback transaction (absent when never borrowed).

PointerPolicy.description: Deterministic policy deciding when the runtime may borrow the real cursor.

oneOf.description: Never touch the real system cursor. Isolated actions that cannot be realized are rejected (`ISOLATED_POINTER_UNAVAILABLE` / `ISOLATED_DRAG_UNAVAILABLE`).
Prefer isolation; allow physical fallback **only when the caller explicitly permits it** for the action (e.g. `physical_fallback: true` on a drag). The default for Pi/OpenCode.
Automatically fall back to the physical cursor when isolation is unavailable. Human input can always interrupt.

RedactedText.description: Redacted description of a `type` action used in traces and logs by default.

Region.description: A rectangle expressed in one of the image-relative coordinate spaces.

RpcRequest.description:
A JSON-RPC 2.0 request as received by the daemon.

`Debug` is redacting by hand: `params` may carry capability tokens (`control_token` / `observation_token` / `admin_token`), so the derived form would print them. `{request:?}` in a log is always safe.

RpcResponse.description:
A JSON-RPC 2.0 response written by the daemon.

`Debug` redacts `result`/`error.data` (the one-time `start` response carries both capability tokens in `result`).

daemon_instance_id.description: Identity of the running daemon instance, generated at startup. A client holding an admin credential compares this against the instance id recorded in its credential file before using it to shut the daemon down — a credential from a different daemon install is stale.

minimum_client_protocol_version.description: Inclusive lower bound of the client protocol versions this daemon accepts. A client below this (or above `maximum_client_protocol_version`) gets `PROTOCOL_VERSION_MISMATCH`.

runtime_version.description: Wire name is `runtime_version` (the protocol spec's field name); the Rust field stays `version` to avoid `version.version`-style confusion.

SessionAction.description: Actions a caller may issue against a session via `computer.session`.

client_id.description: Identity of the client performing the action; recorded on `start`.

control_token.description: The session's control token. Required for `pause`/`resume`/`takeover`/ `release`/`stop`; `start` does not need one. `status` needs either this or the observation token (full status is a sensitive read).

focus_policy.description: Keyboard focus policy for `action: start`. Default `strict` (never steal foreground; Type/Key fail with INPUT_FOCUS_MISMATCH).

observation_token.description: The session's observation token — accepted for `status` in place of the control token.

pointer_policy.description: Pointer isolation policy for `action: start`. Default `isolated_preferred` (never silently borrow the user's cursor).

target.description: Optional app/window target for `action: start`. When set, the session is scoped to that target: observe defaults to it, act rejects coordinates outside it, and keyboard focus is validated against it.

pointer_policy.description: Pointer isolation policy for `action: start`. Default `isolated_preferred` (never silently borrow the user's cursor).

target.description: Optional app/window target for `action: start`. When set, the session is scoped to that target: observe defaults to it, act rejects coordinates outside it, and keyboard focus is validated against it.

control_token.description: The session's control token. **Only present in the `start` response** — it is issued exactly once, on creation, and never repeated by `status` or any other read-only call. Keep it in memory (or the CLI's 0600 credential file), never in logs or traces.

observation_token.description: The session's observation token (read-only capability). **Only present in the `start` response**, like the control token. A holder of only this token can observe/inspect/read traces, but can never act, cancel, pause, or stop.

owner_client_id.description: Who created this session (backward-compatible name of the starting client). The owner_* fields carry the structured identity; only the creating client may stop the session on exit.

SessionState.description: Lifecycle state of a computer-use session.

SessionSummary.description: `session.summary` — the **public** view of the active session. No token needed: it exposes only coarse state and non-secret owner identity. Full `status` (which includes `display_id`, `frame_id`, `trace_dir`) requires an observation or control token.

lock_held.description: True when the session is the control-lock holder.

message.description: Human-readable hint for the common case: the active session is owned by another client.

owner_client_id.description: The non-secret identity of the creating client (name only — never a token, never an instance id or frame/trace paths).

session_id.description: `null` when no session exists — every field is always present on the wire (explicit nulls, never omitted keys): consumers read `summary.session_id == null` without juggling absence.

SessionTarget.description: Optional app/window target for a session. When set, `computer_observe` is scoped to the target window and `computer_act` rejects coordinates outside its bounds. The runtime never auto-clicks other apps.

ShutdownParams.description: `runtime.shutdown` request — requires the daemon admin token.

admin_token.description: The daemon admin token (per-install credential held by the daemon manager — the CLI / LaunchAgent). Ordinary clients never hold it.

StabilizationInfo.description: Outcome of the post-batch stabilization wait (`WaitPolicy::UntilStable`). `change_score` is the **last measured** thumbnail difference — on timeout it carries the real score (never a fabricated 0), so the caller can tell a screen that nearly settled from one that kept animating.

StaleFramePolicy.description: How strictly a referenced `frame_id` must match the current screen.

oneOf.description: Only the **current** frame is actionable. Acting on any older `frame_id` is `STALE_FRAME`, regardless of visual similarity. This is the default: an agent must re-observe between action batches.
Older frames are acceptable as long as the live screen still matches them (visual comparison + app change + age backstop).

TextInputMethod.description: How text is inserted. `keyboard` synthesizes key events with the unicode string; `clipboard` swaps the pasteboard, pastes, and restores it (with a fallback when synthetic key events are unreliable for CJK input).

TraceAdminListParams.description: `trace.admin_list` request — the **daemon-manager** listing across all sessions, authorized by the daemon admin token (never by a session capability). Session tokens must not reveal which other sessions ever ran on the machine; only the operator (CLI / LaunchAgent) may see that.

admin_token.description: The daemon admin token, same credential as `runtime.shutdown`.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest first). Absent = all.

TraceEntry.description: One entry inside a trace file (JSONL).

TraceExportParams.description: `trace.export` request (round 7) — a **pure read**. The daemon never accepts a destination path: exporting a trace requires an observation or control token and returns the content inline (plus its SHA-256), so an observation-capable caller cannot write anywhere through the runtime. Saving the content to a user-chosen location is the client's job.

TraceExportResult.description: `trace.export` result (round 7) — content, never a filesystem path. The daemon performs no filesystem writes for an export; `file_name` is a server-suggested name for a client-side save.

content.description: The trace content itself (redaction applied at record time).

file_name.description: Server-suggested file name (`s_<session_id>.jsonl`) — never a path.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of `content`, so a saved copy can be verified locally.

trace_id.description: Stable id of this trace (one per session — the trace-file stem).

TraceGetParams.description: `trace.get` / `trace.replay` request — trace contents are a sensitive read; an observation or control token is required.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest first). Absent = all.
Maximum entries to return (newest first). Absent = all.

TraceListParams.description: `trace.list` request (round 6): **session-scoped**. A session's capability tokens authorize reads of *that session's* traces only — never a cross-session listing. Verified against the live session, or against the persisted trace access manifest after a daemon restart.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest first). Absent = all.

oneOf.description: A trace write failure fails the operation (session start or act batch).
A trace write failure is logged as degraded but the operation proceeds (the default).
No trace is recorded for this session.

TraceReport.description: Recording status of the session's trace for one `computer.act` batch.

degraded.description: True when the trace could not be written in best-effort mode (or the recorder degraded); the operation itself still succeeded.

warnings.description: Human-readable warnings produced while recording this batch.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest first). Absent = all.
Maximum entries to return (newest first). Absent = all.

TraceSummariesParams.description: `trace.summaries` request — same session-scoped shape and verification as `trace.list`; the response is the raw summary array.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (newest first). Absent = all.

TraceSummary.description: `trace.list` / `trace.summaries` entry — metadata only. The absolute filesystem path never crosses the wire (a path would leak the install layout and invite path-based probing); contents are read via `trace.get` and exported via `trace.export`, both token-gated.

trace_id.description: Stable id of this trace. One trace per session — `trace_id` is the trace-file stem, which is currently the session id.

WaitPolicy.description: What the runtime should do after executing an action batch.

description: JSON-RPC 2.0 wire protocol between the Computer Use daemon and its adapters (SDK, MCP server, Pi extension). Generated from the Rust wire types — edit the Rust source, then run `pnpm generate:protocol`. Capability tokens (control / observation / admin) are 256-bit secrets issued exactly once; the daemon stores only their SHA-256 hashes and never repeats them in responses.
